A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EST research work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, appendices A–E and Algorithm 1 support comparison, including tracking relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting results on four benchmarks, component ablations, sensitivity analyses and temporal-truncation experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds measured computational overhead and attention weights for a worked test query.

M1.justification: The EST components, memory updates, loss and Algorithm 1 are retained. However, Eq. 7 replaces the previously undefined attention input e_t with the elapsed-time projection φ(Δt). The PDFs do not establish whether this changes temporal conditioning or merely clarifies notation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate temporal knowledge graph forecasting on ICEWS14, ICEWS18, ICEWS05-15 and GDELT. The new profiling and worked example use ICEWS14; the million-entity memory estimate is an analytical extrapolation, not an evaluated new dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1's comparator lineup is unchanged. v3 Table 4 newly compares EST-Mamba and EST-Transformer against matched w/o State variants for computational efficiency; v1's efficiency comparison included only the EST backbones.

E3.justification: v3 adds matched resource profiling using seconds per epoch, milliseconds per step and peak memory. Existing splits, training settings and truncation budgets remain unchanged. Although Section 5.1 changes the filtering terminology, Appendix B.3 retains the same explicit chronological, history-only rolling filter.

E4.justification: Adds an ablation isolating persistent-state computational overhead and an ICEWS14 case study tracing retrieved events and attention weights. Existing component, sensitivity, scorer and state-evolution analyses remain. The Mamba truncation analysis moves from Appendix E into Section 5.5 without new results.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are added. Existing gate mean and standard-deviation summaries are unchanged, and the new profiling results provide no additional uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, ablation, scorer and truncation values are unchanged. v3 adds buffer-memory estimates, measured resource results and case-study attention weights. For example, Table 4 reports 60.77 versus 59.60 seconds per epoch for EST-Mamba and its matched stateless control.

T1.justification: Eq. 6 restates the causal-prefix requirement already specified in v1 Appendix D. Existing backbone mathematics and asymptotic bounds are retained. The new buffer-size arithmetic elaborates the previously stated linear memory cost; no substantive theoretical result or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: persistent entity states bridge structure and sequence, counterfactual consistency addresses visibility bias, and EST improves diverse backbones with state-of-the-art forecasting performance.

C2.justification: v3 connects sparse state access and measured overhead to practical scalability, and interprets repeated visits to Iran as evidence in the worked query. Existing limitations concerning memory scaling, unseen entities and real-world nonstationarity are condensed rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies FP32 buffer storage and explains sparse indexing and in-place state updates, alongside additional resource measurements. It removes the code-repository link from the abstract without replacing it elsewhere. Appendix B's hardware, hyperparameters and optimization details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Adds Lin et al. (2026) on ontology-enhanced TKG extrapolation and Liu et al. (2026) on joint knowledge-base completion and question answering. Removes Gastinger et al. (2022), previously cited for evaluation. The substantive related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized revisions rewrite an introduction paragraph and the sequence-backbone explanation, expand efficiency into Section 5.2.1, consolidate temporal-generalization discussion and introduce a worked-example Appendix E. The author/affiliation block and limitations wording also change; most of the document is retained.

P2.justification: Adds resource Tables 3–4 and worked-example Table 11. Former Figures 5 and 6 become one four-panel Figure 5, and existing appendix tables move and are renumbered. Table 1 is reformatted with shaded EST rows; retained plots and numerical displays otherwise preserve their content.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses a gap in v1's efficiency evidence by measuring incremental state costs against matched stateless controls, while the worked query improves explanation of the workflow. These provide modest gains in support and clarity, partly offset by removal of the code-repository pointer. Forecasting evidence remains unchanged, and million-entity scalability is only extrapolated.
